name: The enemies aim at side 0's first slot
result: On the party's core with two MegaMen against BlastMan (layer 3 of --seed 3), side 0's first two slots of BN6_BATTLE_PLAYERS swapped at the battle loop's iteration 300 (the lead's object into slot 1, the partner's into slot 0): BlastMan's next hit, at iteration 377, still struck the lead at column 2 row 2, and every hit after (694, 929, 1417, 1706) struck the partner at column 1 row 1, who stood still. The panels under all three MegaMen held the same flags (0x08410012 from iteration 120), so no occupant's bit tells the lead apart. battle_findPlayer (0x080103BC, BN6_SIDE_PLAYER_GET) walks the side's four slots and returns the first whose NameID it classes as a player (0x0800F29C gives 2); its 149 callers include object_getEnemyPlayerPanels (0x0800D06A), which asks it for the other side; object_getEnemyPlayerPanelY (0x0800D048) has no caller. Then side 0's first slot traded only while an object of side 1's routine runs (BN6_OBJECT_LOGIC_CALL 0x080031FA to BN6_OBJECT_LOGIC_BACK 0x08003200, RunBattleObjectLogic's call), the MegaMan in turn 240 iterations each: three MegaMen against BlastMan took his hits in turn (377 actor 1, 694 actor 2, 929 actor 0, 1417 actor 2, 1692 actor 0, 1955 actor 1, 2415 actor 0), a twin core and 30-frame rollbacks agreeing (56 and 113 of 56 and 113).
meaning: BN6's enemies take their target from side 0's first slot (through battle_findPlayer or the table itself), deciding an attack's aim some frames before it lands. Handing each of side 1's objects, as its routine runs, another MegaMan in that slot spreads a guardian's aim over the party without touching the lead's own place in BN6's tables (src/online/party_field.c, party_field_aim). The spike's earlier answer of battle_findPlayer for enemy callers changed nothing, which this does not explain: its caller test may not have matched.
